name: ambera Theme Builder
author: amberagmbh

sections.description:
Build the whole website with one visual builder — and hand it over without handing over WordPress.

ambera Theme Builder is a page builder and a theme builder in one plugin — and the only one that gives your client a back end of their own. They run the site at /themebuilder/admin/, in plain words, with your logo on top, and never see wp-admin, a plugin list or an update notice. Forms, media, SEO, statistics, security and speed are built in. No Elementor, no stack of add-ons, and no visitor of yours makes a request to somebody else’s server unless you put its address in a page.

Unlock the shop, memberships, courses, appointments, the newsletter, thirty languages and everything else with ambera Pro. Try before you buy: two hours with a site of your own and Pro on it, no install and no account — amberathemebuilder.com/en/try.

Move in from any website

  • Switch from any website. Type the address of the website you have now — on any host, built with any system. ambera reads its start page, lists the pages it links to (up to forty) and rebuilds the ones you tick as drafts here, with their pictures. Its header and footer become the header and footer of this site. “Put everything back” undoes it.
  • Switch from Elementor, Divi or WPBakery. Pages and posts still built with another builder, the block editor or the classic editor are rebuilt from blocks, with their pictures, forms and styles. The old content stays with each page; “Put back” returns it.
  • Set up in three steps. On a fresh site a card leads the way: pick a finished website for your trade, give it your logo and colours, done.
  • Your texts [Pro]. Say what your business does — name, place, offer, for whom, the tone — and the AI rewrites every heading, paragraph and button of the demo in your words and your language, with your own key. It invents no prices, addresses or names, and “Put the demo texts back” returns the originals.

Build professional websites

  • Visual builder. Drag blocks onto the page, style them in a design panel, and see the result at once — on desktop, tablet and phone in the same window.
  • A back end your client can use. Pages, blog, messages, media, forms and statistics in plain words — and no wp-admin behind it.
  • Complete theme builder. Header, footer, single posts, archives, search and 404 in the same editor, with conditions that say where each one applies.
  • 100 blocks, 55 of them free. Layout, text, media, menus, blog, forms — and with Pro a shop, memberships, appointments, events, jobs and downloads.
  • A design system, not a stylesheet. Colours, fonts, spacing and text styles are set once and used everywhere. Change one, and the whole site follows.
  • Work on a page that is already online. Saving keeps a draft; you publish when it suits, now or at a time you set. Two versions side by side, with what changed marked in green, red and orange.

Give clients their own back end

In the editor, a role can be allowed to change words and pictures without being able to move a block. That makes ambera useful for agencies and freelancers — not only while the website is being built, but for the years after it is handed over.

Key features

Everything marked [Pro] is in the separate Pro plugin. Nothing in this free plugin is locked or greyed out.

  • Switch: pages from any other website, or from Elementor, Divi, WPBakery and the block editor, rebuilt from blocks — with a way back.
  • Set up: a finished website for your trade, your logo and colours in three steps; with Pro, the AI writes the texts in your words.
  • Page builder: blocks, a design panel, three screen widths, a layer tree, undo and versions.
  • Theme builder: header and footer free; post, archive, search, 404 and menu templates with Pro.
  • Client area: pages, blog, messages, media, forms, statistics, tasks and users — in plain words, with your logo on top.
  • Access control: per role and per area — see and change, see only, or hidden — down to publishing, deleting and changing an address, and rules for a single page.
  • Forms and inbox: contact, booking and application forms, an inbox with every field, and a log of every mail sent.
  • Media manager: folders, search, cropping, alternative texts — and WebP and AVIF in every size, served to the screen that asked.
  • SEO: titles, descriptions, sitemap, structured data, and a ring on every page that says in per cent what is missing.
  • Statistics: visitors, pages, referrers, devices and countries — counted on your own server, without a cookie or a third party.
  • Security: a firewall in front of every request, a counted sign-in, two-factor authentication with a passkey or an app, hardening, a file scan and a log.
  • Spam protection: five checks under every form, comment and sign-up — a hidden field, a signed clock, a brake per address, a link limit, your own word list. No captcha, no cookie.
  • Speed: finished pages kept as files, images in WebP and AVIF, fonts from your own site. No caching plugin to configure.
  • Tasks and reminders: what has to be done, with a day and a time, and a notice in the client area when it is due.
  • Redirects and 404 list: rules from an old address to a new one, and what visitors asked for and did not get, one click from becoming a rule.
  • Maintenance mode: a switch that closes the site behind a page you designed, while anybody who may edit still sees it.
  • Accessibility: a button visitors use to set the page up for their own eyes — larger text, more contrast, no motion.
  • Shop [Pro]: products with variants and stock, cart, checkout, orders, invoices — Stripe, Payrexx with TWINT, PayPal or on invoice.
  • Memberships and courses [Pro]: sell access monthly, yearly or once; lock a page, a category, a block or a file; courses with a quiz and points.
  • Appointments [Pro]: visitors take a free time themselves — services with a duration, people with their own hours, confirmation and cancellation by email.
  • Events [Pro]: dates many people come to, with places, a price and a waiting list that moves up by itself.
  • Jobs [Pro]: adverts with the details Google Jobs asks for, and the application next to them.
  • Downloads [Pro]: files in groups, under an address that survives replacing the file, counted per day.
  • Reviews [Pro]: the site asks once after an order or an appointment, and you decide what shows.
  • Chatbot [Pro]: a window that answers visitors from your own answers and the pages of the site; what it cannot answer waits for you.
  • Ranking [Pro]: how fast the site is, how Google rates it for search and how the business shows on Google Maps for your keywords — once a day, with a history.
  • Legal pages: an imprint and a privacy policy written from what the site actually does. GDPR for the EU and the EEA.
  • Opening hours: the week, closed days and public holidays in one place, shown by the blocks “Opening hours” and “Next date”.
  • Newsletter [Pro]: written with the same blocks as a page, sent from the site itself, with lists, double opt-in, opens and clicks.
  • Thirty languages [Pro]: /fr/contact is a real page — translated on first view, then stored, with hreflang.
  • Custom fields [Pro]: sets of fields per kind of post, written into a template by a block.
  • AI assistance [Pro]: a section, a whole page, a blog post or a picture from a description — with your own key.
  • AI tools over MCP [Pro]: Claude, Cursor or Codex build pages here as real blocks, through one key you hand out and take back.
  • Backups: the whole site in one file, on a plan, checked after every run, restored with one click.
  • Snippets [Pro]: CSS, JavaScript or HTML with a name, a place and a condition, instead of another plugin.
  • Early firewall [Pro]: the rules load before WordPress does, for every file of the site.
  • Country blocking: whole countries allowed or turned away.

The 55 free blocks

Layout: Page, Section, Grid, Column, Flex row, Group, Spacer, Divider, Off canvas, Loop carousel.

Text and buttons: Heading, Text, List, Quote, Button, Icon, Icon card, Shortcode.

Media: Image, Gallery, Video, Slider, Slide, Flip box, Before and after.

People and proof: Team, Person, Reviews, Review, Portfolio, Share buttons, Profiles, PayPal button.

The site around the page: Site name, Logo, Menu, Menu entry, Link list, Breadcrumbs, Sitemap, Search, Results, Light and dark, Contents, Opening hours, Next date, Locations, One location.

Blog: Post title, Post image, Post details, Post content, Post list.

Forms: Form, Field.

Pro features

Pro is a separate plugin for professional, multilingual and commercial websites, bought once per number of websites, with a year of updates and support. It adds thirteen modules and 45 blocks to the same editor.

Pro modules

  • Shop: categories, CSV import, six customer emails with a designer, invoices and credit notes.
  • Memberships and courses: free plans, trials, and renewals that run by themselves.
  • Appointments: a break after each service, days off, and per service free slots or a request.
  • Events: sign-up without an account, and confirmations with a calendar file and a link that cancels.
  • Jobs: a screen that says what is still missing, and application papers behind an address that asks first.
  • Downloads: files that can be locked to members.
  • Reviews: written without an account; nothing shows until you let it through.
  • Newsletter: sending in batches at a time you choose, with header, footer and content templates.
  • Thirty languages: every language its own address, and corrections that survive a retranslation.
  • Custom fields: filled in by whoever writes the post.
  • AI: nothing runs without your own key.
  • Connections (MCP): reading or writing, no access to users, orders, settings or files, every change undoable.
  • Snippets: an error stays with the snippet instead of taking the page down.

Pro blocks

  • Content: Carousel, Popup, Table, Figure, Accordion, Accordion entry, Tabs, Tab, HTML, Price, Price switch, Currency switch, Countdown, Timeline, Station.
  • Media: Google Maps, Facebook embed, Video playlist, Video in the list, Image hotspots, Point.
  • Shop: Products, Product, Cart, Cart button, Checkout, Account.
  • Memberships and courses: Memberships, Members only, Course, Courses, Learning points, Save it, Saved and seen.
  • Modules: Appointment, Events, One event, Event calendar, Jobs, One job, Downloads, Download button, Newsletter, Unsubscribe, Custom field, Languages.

Build the whole website

One editor covers everything a visitor sees, down to the reusable parts used on many pages at once. Sections, groups and columns can end in a shape instead of a straight line — a wave, a slant, a triangle, mountains — drawn in the page, so nothing is loaded and nothing is blurry.

Start with a complete demo website

Thirty-five finished websites come free: a bakery, a hotel, a restaurant, a photographer, a law firm, an architect, a yoga studio, a wedding planner and more — each one a different trade and a different look. One click installs a demo with its pages, templates, menus and pictures; another click removes it completely.

External services

Each service is called only in the situation named, never in the background. Besides the request itself, WordPress sends its version and the site address.

  • Demo catalogue (amberathemebuilder.com, by the plugin author): the demo screen loads the list and preview pictures from https://amberathemebuilder.com/katalog/demos.json; installing a demo downloads its zip. No personal data. Terms, privacy.
  • Google Fonts (fonts.google.com, fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com): fetching a font, installing a demo, importing HTML or picking a font not stored yet sends the family name to https://fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts/ and downloads the font once into your uploads. The tick “Show what they look like” (off by default) loads samples into your own browser, which sends your IP address to Google. Visitors never contact Google. Terms, privacy.
  • Pixabay (pixabay.com): only with your own API key. A search sends the words and the key to https://pixabay.com/api/; a picked photo is downloaded. Terms, privacy.
  • Country lookup (api.country.is): off by default. Switched on under Statistics or Firewall → Countries, the IP address of a visitor whose country no CDN header gives is sent once to https://api.country.is/; the answer is kept a week under a hash. Privacy, source.
  • YouTube and Vimeo: the video block and the help videos load the player from youtube-nocookie.com or player.vimeo.com only after a click on play. YouTube terms, Google privacy, Vimeo terms, Vimeo privacy.
  • Google Maps (maps.google.com): the Locations block loads the map for the address you entered only after a visitor clicks. Terms, privacy.
  • PayPal (paypal.com): the PayPal block is a plain form to https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr; a visitor’s click sends what you entered in the block (PayPal address, item, amount, currency, return address). Agreement, privacy.
  • Share links (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Pinterest): plain links; a click sends the page address and title. Meta, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Pinterest.
  • Support portal (portal.amberathemebuilder.com): “Support ticket” and “Feature request” on the Help screen are links; the link prefills host name, plugin, WordPress and PHP version and site language. The plugin never calls the portal. Terms, privacy.
  • Imported HTML and Switch → “From another website”: while you import a template or press “Look at the site” and “Switch these pages”, your server fetches the pages, images, stylesheets and fonts they name from the server they name, and an import sends one HEAD request to each video address, which keeps playing from there. Only the request is sent, with the plugin version as user agent. Addresses on your own server or in a private network are refused.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the plugin directory.
  2. Activate it under Plugins.
  3. Open ambera in the admin menu. The dashboard walks you through the first steps: pick a demo or start blank, set your colours and fonts, edit the header and footer.
  4. Set up the client area if someone else will run the website.

The plugin brings its own theme layer. If you keep another theme active, ambera renders the pages you assign to it and leaves the rest to the theme.
sections.faq:
Is ambera Theme Builder free?

Yes. This plugin is free and complete: the builder, the theme layer, the client area, forms, media, SEO, statistics, redirects, security, spam protection, tasks and thirty-five demo websites. There is no key, no account and no trial period.

What is the difference between Free and Pro?

Free builds and runs a whole website — including legal pages, backups and country blocking. Pro adds what a commercial or multilingual site needs: shop, memberships and courses, appointments, events, jobs, downloads, reviews, newsletter, thirty languages, custom fields, AI, editable templates for posts and archives, more blocks. See the feature comparison.

Do I need Elementor, Divi or another page builder?

No. ambera has its own visual builder for pages and for the theme around them. It is not an add-on for another builder.

Do I still need a theme?

No. ambera renders header, footer and every template itself. A block theme can stay installed — WordPress needs one to be active, and ambera works with any.

Can I use ambera for client websites?

Yes, and that is what it is built for. The client area gives the people who run the site a back end of their own, and you decide what they may change.

Can clients manage their website without wp-admin?

Yes. Pages, blog, messages, media, forms, statistics and users are in the client area, in plain words. The WordPress dashboard stays with you.

Can I import a complete website?

Yes. Thirty-five demo websites install with one click, with pages, templates, menus and pictures, and can be removed just as easily.

Does it work with the block editor (Gutenberg)?

Yes. Posts written in the block editor are shown inside the templates you build. Pages can be built with either editor; ambera’s editor is used for the layout of the site itself. Posts can also be written in the classic WordPress editor.

Does the plugin send anything home?

Nothing without your action. There is no tracking and no licence check — this plugin has no key, no account and no licence server; updates come from wordpress.org through WordPress’ own update check. The demo catalogue, Google Fonts, the stock-photo search, the files an HTML import names and the pages of a website you switch from are loaded only when you open those screens or press those buttons; see “External services”.

Is the statistics module GDPR-friendly?

It counts on your server, sets no cookie and stores no IP address. The visitor’s country comes from your CDN’s header if there is one; the optional lookup at an external service is off by default.

Can I switch an existing site built with Elementor or Divi?

Yes. The screen “Switch” lists every page and post still built with Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, the block editor or the classic editor, and rebuilds each one from blocks — read as it stands on the site, with its pictures, forms and styles. Leave the old builder active until the switch is through. The old content stays with every page, and “Put back” returns it.

Moving from a website that stands somewhere else? Under “From another website” on the same screen, give its address: the plugin reads its start page, lists the pages it links to (up to 40), and rebuilds the ones you tick as drafts here, with their pictures; the header and footer of the start page become the header and footer of this site. Nothing is fetched until you press the buttons, and “Put everything back” moves the drafts to the trash.

The Legal module added its entry to the menu before the ambera menu itself was there; WordPress then took that entry for the first one, could not find its page and made a plain file link of it — for the entry and for “ambera” above it. The ambera menu is now set up before any module adds to it, and every entry opens its screen.

0.4.15

  • Switching on Pro next to the free version left Pro doing nothing. The two are the same plugin under two names, and WordPress loads “ambera-theme-builder” before “ambera-theme” — so the free version always started first, claimed the plugin’s folder, and Pro’s own code never ran: no shop, no Pro blocks, four warnings in the log on every request. Pro now switches the free version off as it is switched on, and the free version steps aside whenever Pro is on — which also puts right every site on which both have been on since 0.4.14.
  • Deleting the free version after moving to Pro deleted your settings. Both versions share every setting and every table, and the free version’s clean-up removed them all: licence key, design, SEO texts, statistics. Deleting one version now leaves all of it in place as long as the other is still installed; deleting the last one cleans up as before.

0.4.14

  • Legal pages are free: an imprint and a privacy policy from what the site does, as drafts you edit like any page — GDPR, with the duties of Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
  • Backups are free: the whole site in one file, now or on a plan, full or only what changed, back with one click.
  • Country blocking is free; the early firewall stays with Pro.
  • The page cache keeps its pages when the site is visited in another language.
  • A dash in a page title reaches search engines and the SEO screen as one character.

0.4.13

  • Four new blocks: Opening hours, Contents (a table of contents from the headings), Before and after, and Locations (several addresses with one map).
  • The menu of the client area is sorted into areas that fold away.
  • Deleting the plugin removes its settings, tables, roles, scheduled jobs and files; people with its roles become editors or subscribers. Settings › General decides whether backups and personal records go too; pages, templates and forms stay.
  • “Build the page cache” tries each page twice and names the ones that do not answer.
  • Statistics keeps accents in city names (Zürich).
  • Text typed straight into an empty block is saved without the editor’s placeholder; descriptions for screen readers take no space on the page.

0.4.12

  • Translations updated.
  • The rest of this version is Pro.

0.4.11

  • An update that cannot succeed is refused before anything is deleted. WordPress clears the old plugin folder first and only notices halfway through when it is not allowed to — what is left is a folder without its main file, which WordPress no longer recognises as a plugin: it drops out of the list, switches off, and the site stands there without its theme. The plugin now looks over its own folders first and stops the update with a message naming the one in the way, so the running version stays and the site keeps working.
  • A plugin folder that is only a link to somewhere else is refused as well. Updating it would rewrite the files it points at — where several sites share one folder, that takes down the sites nobody touched.

0.4.10

  • Help now has a chapter for every part of the plugin, the ones that come with Pro included — so the screen tells you what a thing does before you have to decide whether you need it. Each chapter has its own films where one exists.
  • The rest of this version happens in Pro; the free plugin keeps step with it.

0.4.9

  • Support without an account. “Support ticket” and “Feature request” on the Help screen used to open a sign-in page — the free plugin has no account there. They now lead to an open form: you write your question, the answer comes by email, and you answer by replying to it. Version, WordPress, PHP and the site are filled in before you arrive, and screenshots may come along.
  • A header template can stay at the top while the page scrolls, so the menu and the search stay within reach on a long page. The switch sits on the template, beside “Lies over the content”.

0.4.8

  • Tasks are part of the free plugin now: what has to be done, with a day and a time, and a reminder in the client area when it is due.
  • The post list can carry filter buttons — one for each category among the posts shown — and filters without loading the page again.
  • The search block can suggest matching pages while a visitor types.
  • The Security screen has tabs instead of seven sections under one another; one button still saves the whole screen.
  • The builder is set in Open Sans. The font ships with the plugin; nothing is fetched from Google.
  • Fixed: “No programs in the uploads folder” took a file written by an earlier version for a stranger’s and asked the owner to edit the .htaccess by hand.
  • Fixed: where that file really belongs to somebody else, the rule now goes in as its own block between two marker lines, the way WordPress writes its own.

0.4.7

  • Spam protection under every form, every comment and every sign-up: a hidden field, a signed clock, a brake per address, a limit on links and a word list of your own. No captcha, nothing from Google, no cookie.
  • Sections, groups, columns and grids can end in a shape instead of a straight line — a wave, a slant, a triangle, mountains — drawn in the page, so nothing is loaded and nothing is blurry.

0.4.6

  • The date a page was last changed follows its layout, which is what search engines and caches read.

0.4.4 – 0.4.5

  • Compatibility improvements and internal hooks.

0.4.3

  • Compatibility improvements and internal hooks.

0.4.2

  • Two-factor sign-in keeps “Remember me”: the tick on the first form now survives the code on the second.

0.4.0 – 0.4.1

  • Compatibility improvements and internal hooks.

0.3.7

  • A button can lead to a file from the media library (a download).

0.3.5 – 0.3.6, 0.3.8 – 0.3.9

  • Compatibility improvements and internal hooks.

  • The early firewall (loader in the site root) is a Pro file; the free plugin writes nothing outside the uploads folder.
  • The residual stylesheet of an HTML import is kept only with its checker, which is Pro; the free plugin drops it.
  • External services: PayPal button and share links are documented.

  • Drawings and icons are escaped; an uploaded demo package is checked file by file.

short_description: Build a whole WordPress website visually — or move yours in from any other site — with a client area, forms, media, SEO and statistics.
description:
Build the whole website with one visual builder — and hand it over without handing over WordPress.

ambera Theme Builder is a page builder and a theme builder in one plugin — and the only one that gives your client a back end of their own. They run the site at /themebuilder/admin/, in plain words, with your logo on top, and never see wp-admin, a plugin list or an update notice. Forms, media, SEO, statistics, security and speed are built in. No Elementor, no stack of add-ons, and no visitor of yours makes a request to somebody else’s server unless you put its address in a page.

Unlock the shop, memberships, courses, appointments, the newsletter, thirty languages and everything else with ambera Pro. Try before you buy: two hours with a site of your own and Pro on it, no install and no account — amberathemebuilder.com/en/try.

Move in from any website

  • Switch from any website. Type the address of the website you have now — on any host, built with any system. ambera reads its start page, lists the pages it links to (up to forty) and rebuilds the ones you tick as drafts here, with their pictures. Its header and footer become the header and footer of this site. “Put everything back” undoes it.
  • Switch from Elementor, Divi or WPBakery. Pages and posts still built with another builder, the block editor or the classic editor are rebuilt from blocks, with their pictures, forms and styles. The old content stays with each page; “Put back” returns it.
  • Set up in three steps. On a fresh site a card leads the way: pick a finished website for your trade, give it your logo and colours, done.
  • Your texts [Pro]. Say what your business does — name, place, offer, for whom, the tone — and the AI rewrites every heading, paragraph and button of the demo in your words and your language, with your own key. It invents no prices, addresses or names, and “Put the demo texts back” returns the originals.

Build professional websites

  • Visual builder. Drag blocks onto the page, style them in a design panel, and see the result at once — on desktop, tablet and phone in the same window.
  • A back end your client can use. Pages, blog, messages, media, forms and statistics in plain words — and no wp-admin behind it.
  • Complete theme builder. Header, footer, single posts, archives, search and 404 in the same editor, with conditions that say where each one applies.
  • 100 blocks, 55 of them free. Layout, text, media, menus, blog, forms — and with Pro a shop, memberships, appointments, events, jobs and downloads.
  • A design system, not a stylesheet. Colours, fonts, spacing and text styles are set once and used everywhere. Change one, and the whole site follows.
  • Work on a page that is already online. Saving keeps a draft; you publish when it suits, now or at a time you set. Two versions side by side, with what changed marked in green, red and orange.

Give clients their own back end

In the editor, a role can be allowed to change words and pictures without being able to move a block. That makes ambera useful for agencies and freelancers — not only while the website is being built, but for the years after it is handed over.

Key features

Everything marked [Pro] is in the separate Pro plugin. Nothing in this free plugin is locked or greyed out.

  • Switch: pages from any other website, or from Elementor, Divi, WPBakery and the block editor, rebuilt from blocks — with a way back.
  • Set up: a finished website for your trade, your logo and colours in three steps; with Pro, the AI writes the texts in your words.
  • Page builder: blocks, a design panel, three screen widths, a layer tree, undo and versions.
  • Theme builder: header and footer free; post, archive, search, 404 and menu templates with Pro.
  • Client area: pages, blog, messages, media, forms, statistics, tasks and users — in plain words, with your logo on top.
  • Access control: per role and per area — see and change, see only, or hidden — down to publishing, deleting and changing an address, and rules for a single page.
  • Forms and inbox: contact, booking and application forms, an inbox with every field, and a log of every mail sent.
  • Media manager: folders, search, cropping, alternative texts — and WebP and AVIF in every size, served to the screen that asked.
  • SEO: titles, descriptions, sitemap, structured data, and a ring on every page that says in per cent what is missing.
  • Statistics: visitors, pages, referrers, devices and countries — counted on your own server, without a cookie or a third party.
  • Security: a firewall in front of every request, a counted sign-in, two-factor authentication with a passkey or an app, hardening, a file scan and a log.
  • Spam protection: five checks under every form, comment and sign-up — a hidden field, a signed clock, a brake per address, a link limit, your own word list. No captcha, no cookie.
  • Speed: finished pages kept as files, images in WebP and AVIF, fonts from your own site. No caching plugin to configure.
  • Tasks and reminders: what has to be done, with a day and a time, and a notice in the client area when it is due.
  • Redirects and 404 list: rules from an old address to a new one, and what visitors asked for and did not get, one click from becoming a rule.
  • Maintenance mode: a switch that closes the site behind a page you designed, while anybody who may edit still sees it.
  • Accessibility: a button visitors use to set the page up for their own eyes — larger text, more contrast, no motion.
  • Shop [Pro]: products with variants and stock, cart, checkout, orders, invoices — Stripe, Payrexx with TWINT, PayPal or on invoice.
  • Memberships and courses [Pro]: sell access monthly, yearly or once; lock a page, a category, a block or a file; courses with a quiz and points.
  • Appointments [Pro]: visitors take a free time themselves — services with a duration, people with their own hours, confirmation and cancellation by email.
  • Events [Pro]: dates many people come to, with places, a price and a waiting list that moves up by itself.
  • Jobs [Pro]: adverts with the details Google Jobs asks for, and the application next to them.
  • Downloads [Pro]: files in groups, under an address that survives replacing the file, counted per day.
  • Reviews [Pro]: the site asks once after an order or an appointment, and you decide what shows.
  • Chatbot [Pro]: a window that answers visitors from your own answers and the pages of the site; what it cannot answer waits for you.
  • Ranking [Pro]: how fast the site is, how Google rates it for search and how the business shows on Google Maps for your keywords — once a day, with a history.
  • Legal pages: an imprint and a privacy policy written from what the site actually does. GDPR for the EU and the EEA.
  • Opening hours: the week, closed days and public holidays in one place, shown by the blocks “Opening hours” and “Next date”.
  • Newsletter [Pro]: written with the same blocks as a page, sent from the site itself, with lists, double opt-in, opens and clicks.
  • Thirty languages [Pro]: /fr/contact is a real page — translated on first view, then stored, with hreflang.
  • Custom fields [Pro]: sets of fields per kind of post, written into a template by a block.
  • AI assistance [Pro]: a section, a whole page, a blog post or a picture from a description — with your own key.
  • AI tools over MCP [Pro]: Claude, Cursor or Codex build pages here as real blocks, through one key you hand out and take back.
  • Backups: the whole site in one file, on a plan, checked after every run, restored with one click.
  • Snippets [Pro]: CSS, JavaScript or HTML with a name, a place and a condition, instead of another plugin.
  • Early firewall [Pro]: the rules load before WordPress does, for every file of the site.
  • Country blocking: whole countries allowed or turned away.

The 55 free blocks

Layout: Page, Section, Grid, Column, Flex row, Group, Spacer, Divider, Off canvas, Loop carousel.

Text and buttons: Heading, Text, List, Quote, Button, Icon, Icon card, Shortcode.

Media: Image, Gallery, Video, Slider, Slide, Flip box, Before and after.

People and proof: Team, Person, Reviews, Review, Portfolio, Share buttons, Profiles, PayPal button.

The site around the page: Site name, Logo, Menu, Menu entry, Link list, Breadcrumbs, Sitemap, Search, Results, Light and dark, Contents, Opening hours, Next date, Locations, One location.

Blog: Post title, Post image, Post details, Post content, Post list.

Forms: Form, Field.

Pro features

Pro is a separate plugin for professional, multilingual and commercial websites, bought once per number of websites, with a year of updates and support. It adds thirteen modules and 45 blocks to the same editor.

Pro modules

  • Shop: categories, CSV import, six customer emails with a designer, invoices and credit notes.
  • Memberships and courses: free plans, trials, and renewals that run by themselves.
  • Appointments: a break after each service, days off, and per service free slots or a request.
  • Events: sign-up without an account, and confirmations with a calendar file and a link that cancels.
  • Jobs: a screen that says what is still missing, and application papers behind an address that asks first.
  • Downloads: files that can be locked to members.
  • Reviews: written without an account; nothing shows until you let it through.
  • Newsletter: sending in batches at a time you choose, with header, footer and content templates.
  • Thirty languages: every language its own address, and corrections that survive a retranslation.
  • Custom fields: filled in by whoever writes the post.
  • AI: nothing runs without your own key.
  • Connections (MCP): reading or writing, no access to users, orders, settings or files, every change undoable.
  • Snippets: an error stays with the snippet instead of taking the page down.

Pro blocks

  • Content: Carousel, Popup, Table, Figure, Accordion, Accordion entry, Tabs, Tab, HTML, Price, Price switch, Currency switch, Countdown, Timeline, Station.
  • Media: Google Maps, Facebook embed, Video playlist, Video in the list, Image hotspots, Point.
  • Shop: Products, Product, Cart, Cart button, Checkout, Account.
  • Memberships and courses: Memberships, Members only, Course, Courses, Learning points, Save it, Saved and seen.
  • Modules: Appointment, Events, One event, Event calendar, Jobs, One job, Downloads, Download button, Newsletter, Unsubscribe, Custom field, Languages.

Build the whole website

One editor covers everything a visitor sees, down to the reusable parts used on many pages at once. Sections, groups and columns can end in a shape instead of a straight line — a wave, a slant, a triangle, mountains — drawn in the page, so nothing is loaded and nothing is blurry.

Start with a complete demo website

Thirty-five finished websites come free: a bakery, a hotel, a restaurant, a photographer, a law firm, an architect, a yoga studio, a wedding planner and more — each one a different trade and a different look. One click installs a demo with its pages, templates, menus and pictures; another click removes it completely.

External services

Each service is called only in the situation named, never in the background. Besides the request itself, WordPress sends its version and the site address.

  • Demo catalogue (amberathemebuilder.com, by the plugin author): the demo screen loads the list and preview pictures from https://amberathemebuilder.com/katalog/demos.json; installing a demo downloads its zip. No personal data. Terms, privacy.
  • Google Fonts (fonts.google.com, fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com): fetching a font, installing a demo, importing HTML or picking a font not stored yet sends the family name to https://fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts/ and downloads the font once into your uploads. The tick “Show what they look like” (off by default) loads samples into your own browser, which sends your IP address to Google. Visitors never contact Google. Terms, privacy.
  • Pixabay (pixabay.com): only with your own API key. A search sends the words and the key to https://pixabay.com/api/; a picked photo is downloaded. Terms, privacy.
  • Country lookup (api.country.is): off by default. Switched on under Statistics or Firewall → Countries, the IP address of a visitor whose country no CDN header gives is sent once to https://api.country.is/; the answer is kept a week under a hash. Privacy, source.
  • YouTube and Vimeo: the video block and the help videos load the player from youtube-nocookie.com or player.vimeo.com only after a click on play. YouTube terms, Google privacy, Vimeo terms, Vimeo privacy.
  • Google Maps (maps.google.com): the Locations block loads the map for the address you entered only after a visitor clicks. Terms, privacy.
  • PayPal (paypal.com): the PayPal block is a plain form to https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr; a visitor’s click sends what you entered in the block (PayPal address, item, amount, currency, return address). Agreement, privacy.
  • Share links (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Pinterest): plain links; a click sends the page address and title. Meta, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Pinterest.
  • Support portal (portal.amberathemebuilder.com): “Support ticket” and “Feature request” on the Help screen are links; the link prefills host name, plugin, WordPress and PHP version and site language. The plugin never calls the portal. Terms, privacy.
  • Imported HTML and Switch → “From another website”: while you import a template or press “Look at the site” and “Switch these pages”, your server fetches the pages, images, stylesheets and fonts they name from the server they name, and an import sends one HEAD request to each video address, which keeps playing from there. Only the request is sent, with the plugin version as user agent. Addresses on your own server or in a private network are refused.
